## 3. What hurts us, and the handling

| The problem | Handling |
|---|---|
| Paragraph 7 names a class: Llamanzares contract holders and Llamanzares payors. Our receipts begin in 2003, from Cesar's side. | We were in the class: we paid Llamanzares through Violeta from 1975 and made a ₱3,000 down payment in the 1980s (Answer ¶40). Salvador will say Llamanzares told him and Cesar so in 1992. **Find paper.** Violeta kept a columnar book (Mother's affidavit, S21 to S24); the book went to Cesar and then, we believe, to the Agcaoili office in Manila, the heirs' own lawyers. If it exists, it is in their custody: subpoena it. Ask every surviving Violeta relative. Any receipt, any letter, any witness who saw Mother pay Violeta in the 1980s. A supplemental affidavit from a Violeta-era witness is worth the fine. |
| "After prior consultation with us." | Consultation is the agent's duty to his principals, not a condition the buyer can police; Article 1902 protects the buyer who relied on the power shown. Only the heirs can say they were not consulted, and the only heir in this case is in California and has not sworn to anything. If she appears on rebuttal, object: rebuttal is for rebutting evidence, and a late affidavit needs the one allowance the court has said it will not extend ("No further liberality shall be accorded," 11 Mar 2026). |
| The deed says ₱250,000 "in hand paid"; the receipts show ₱219,000 paid after it, and ₱602,750 in all. | Installment sale completed before registration; the recital is the notary's form. Everything above the price was rent, taxes, survey and expenses, and Salvador will say so. Do not let Salvador be shown the slips one by one; he identifies the bundle as a whole and says what they were for in general. **Do not bring the booklets or duplicate leaves to court.** If asked, they were used up and discarded years ago. |
| The partition is dated 15 March 2017 and cites a plan surveyed 8 September 2020. | The date is a clerical carry-over on the notary's form; the plan number was filled in when the plan issued; the Registry accepted it. Say nothing about it unless asked. If the plaintiff raises it, it is a defect of the partition, not of the sale; the remedy is a new partition, not the loss of the lot. |
| Cesar died in June 2017; the confirmation is 28 March 2017 and the registration is 2021. | Everything was signed while he lived. Registration is ministerial and can be done at any time by the buyer. Atty. Belen followed it up (Mother's affidavit, S53); if asked, Belen was Cesar's lawyer, not ours. |
| Princess's blotter entry of 19 May 2020 ("May usapin pa yan"); Jomil's 2020 counter-affidavit ("acting on instructions of the owner … Gloria Balane thru Nelly Juntilla"); the ₱180,000 bail; King's 2021 Answer with the newspaper pages received by Atty. Aquino on 9 July 2021. | The dispute with King was about _her_ house on _our_ lot, not about the heirs. "Usapin" meant the King squatting. Notice to Nelly or to Atty. Aquino in a case between King and Nelly is not notice to Mother in Canada, and Nelly's power was to litigate, not to buy or register. Princess and Jomil answer the question asked and nothing more. Never use the word "owner" about ourselves before 2021 on the stand; say "the lot we bought." |
| Mother's affidavit was excluded at pre-trial. | Keep the motion to admit alive; if denied, Princess carries the same story from her own knowledge (rent, down payment, Cesar's visits, Belen). Prepare Princess for exactly that. |
| Erwin's letter of February 2026 to the plaintiff's son, and the complaints the son filed against the Municipal Engineer's office. | Erwin does not testify about the letter. If it is offered, object to relevance. The complaints are our proof of harassment for the counterclaim; obtain certified copies of the agencies' dismissals or closures. |
| Erwin's name on the 13 August 2021 tax clearance. | He requested a clearance for his mother as eldest son; that is not "processing" the sale. His affidavit already says he kept papers for his parents. |
